name: Otemachi
tagline: Tokyo in 1 minute and Otemachi in 1 minute. Served by 5 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥160,000 to ¥170,000.
summary: The station is in Chiyoda City, where Tokyo Metro and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 5 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 1 minute to Otemachi, 19 minutes to Shinjuku, 19 minutes to Shibuya and 16 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥160,000 to ¥170,000. The station stands 3 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 3.9 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 3 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 0.5 m to 4.4 m, a difference of 3.9 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls inside the projected inundation area, to a projected depth of less than 0.5 m. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 7 also fall inside the area, and the deepest projection is 0.5 to 3 m. For storm surge, 7 of the nine points also fall inside the projected area. On the whole, the flood projection here is about average for the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 8 clinics and 7 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 宮内庁病院, about 7 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 同仁記念会明和病院, about 20 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 5 lines serve the station. Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line run through it. Tokyo Metro Tozai Line also call here. Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line are available too. Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line stop here as well. Toei Mita Line stop here as well. The lines are split between operators (Tokyo Metro runs 4 lines and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Tozai Line runs at 160% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 木場→門前仲町, which this station is not on. Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line runs at 154%. Its busiest stretch is 新大塚→茗荷谷, which this station is likewise not on. Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line runs at 150%. Its busiest stretch is 町屋→西日暮里, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥160,000 to ¥170,000 and 1K ¥150,000 to ¥160,000. 1LDK ¥250,000 to ¥260,000 and 2LDK ¥320,000 to ¥330,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥160,000 to ¥170,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the low side. 5 lines and a wide choice of connections pushes the figure up. On the other side, many bars by the station and voices outside late at night holds it down. For 1LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Tokyo is ahead on the number of lines, but Otemachi is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Otemachi. Tokyo has 10 lines that Otemachi does not. With more lines, Tokyo is the better connected of the two. To Shinagawa, for instance, Tokyo is 6 minutes quicker. A one-room flat also costs about ¥7,000 less at Tokyo.

neighbours.lead: Otemachi is ahead on the number of lines.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Otemachi. Nijubashimae has only the Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line, so Otemachi is the better connected. To Tokyo, for instance, Nijubashimae takes 6 minutes longer. Rents, flood projections and the rest differ little.

noiseSources: The 首都高速都心環状線 viaduct runs a short walk from the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
永代通り (a main road) runs right beside the station, so for a flat close to the station, check whether it faces the road

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 5 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself sits inside the area projected to flood in the heaviest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 5 lines serve the station, and the choice of connections is wider than at most stations in the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: The big roads are far enough that traffic noise is unlikely to bother you.
